articles.title: Petrol, diesel prices rose 7% in India vs 50-70% globally over four years: Hardeep Puri
articles.titleEn: Petrol, diesel prices rose 7% in India vs 50-70% globally over four years: Hardeep Puri
articles.summary: Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri announced that fuel prices in India have risen by just 7% over four years. The government implemented three reductions in central excise duty, helping maintain stable prices. Puri criticized rumors of an LPG shortage, emphasizing increased domestic production of LPG. Challenges from international conflicts and geopolitical tensions still persist, affecting the crude oil market.

articles.title: Petrol, diesel prices rose just 7% in India over four years against 50-70% global surge: Hardeep Puri
articles.titleEn: Petrol, diesel prices rose just 7% in India over four years against 50-70% global surge: Hardeep Puri
articles.summary: “India is a unique case globally. Thanks to the Prime Minister’s hands-on policy, the central excise duty has been reduced three times: in November 2021, May 2022, and on March 10, 2026. Prices did not rise. In fact, if you look at a four-year reference period, prices in India have actually decreased. Meanwhile, elsewhere in the world, petrol and diesel prices surged by 50–70%, whereas in India, they increased by only 7%,” Puri told reporters in Indore.
